memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the offerings you are to receive from them: gold, silver and bronze; blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen; goat hair; ram skins dyed red and another type of durable leather; acacia wood; olive oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense; and onyx stones and other gems to be mounted on the ephod and breastpiece." - Exodus 25:3-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look at the wonderful variety in this list. Gold and silver, yes — but also goat hair. Precious gems, but also wood and oil and thread. Some Israelites had jewellery to give; others had only spun yarn or a few skins. God asked for all of it, and every contribution had its place in the finished tabernacle.

There is real encouragement here. God's work is not built only by the wealthy or the impressive. The person who brought goat hair was as essential as the one who brought onyx stones. The curtains needed yarn; the lamps needed oil. Nothing offered to God was too ordinary to be useful in His hands.

The same is true in His church today. Some have gifts that shine visibly, others serve in ways no one notices. But Paul reminds us that the body has many parts, and the parts that seem less impressive are actually indispensable (1 Cor 12:22). Do not disqualify yourself because your offering seems plain. God is building something beautiful, and He has a place for exactly what you have to bring. What is in your hands today that God might be asking for?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I ever disqualify myself because my gifts seem too ordinary?
What has God placed in my hands that I could offer for His work?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that nothing offered to You is too ordinary to be useful. Help me bring what I have without comparing, trusting You to use it in Your good work. Amen.
